The proposed scheme employs elliptic curve cryptography to ensure security and privacy in a distributed manner for the transmission of medical text data.

The scheme avoids expensive operations like bilinear pairing and map-to-point hash functions, and instead uses point addition, XOR operations, and one-way hash functions to reduce the computational burden.
The scheme provides protection to both the random part and the secret key part of the authenticated ciphertext data, achieving full privacy preservation.

The scheme adopts a distributed key generation methodology and aggregation technique to alleviate the central tendency over medical servers, reducing the computation and communication costs during signature verification.
The scheme is resistant to existential signature forgery attacks, man-in-the-middle attacks, and other attacks, as proven under the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem (ECDLP).
The proposed scheme reduces the computational overhead by 93% compared to existing schemes due to the incorporation of aggregation technology.
The communication cost of the proposed scheme is 400 bits, which is a significant reduction compared to its counterparts.

The scheme achieves message authentication, integrity, traceability, and anonymity, making it potentially applicable to other resource-constrained IoT environments beyond healthcare wearable wireless medical sensor networks.
The scheme employs a distributed approach to key generation and signature verification, avoiding reliance on a centralized medical server and fully preserving user privacy.
The scheme's use of elliptic curve cryptography provides a highly effective technique that is more efficient than bilinear pairing operations commonly used in existing schemes.
The scheme's design goals include ensuring data integrity, message authentication, confidentiality, anonymity, forward and backward secrecy, and unlinkability during data collection and transmission.

The resource-constrained nature of IoT devices, the vulnerability of the open wireless communication channel to attacks, and the need to ensure various security and privacy properties are the main challenges addressed by the proposed scheme.
The scheme's formal and informal security analysis demonstrates its resistance to various attacks, including existential signature forgery, man-in-the-middle, and other attacks.
The scheme's performance analysis shows significant improvements in computational overhead, communication cost, and signature verification time compared to existing schemes.

The proposed scheme's features, such as message authentication, integrity, traceability, and anonymity, make it potentially applicable to other resource-constrained IoT environments, such as vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs) and wireless body area networks (WBANs).
